item.text:
**7B.8 Assessment:** mixed, leaning negative. Marcos showed some procedural restraint and institutional responses, but the year also featured incomplete promise-keeping, misleading public framing on rice, and a still-coercive information environment.

**Supports 7B.8**
- [PBBM says Comelec has mandate to probe alleged signature-buying for PI](/https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217440) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-23 | Claim: Marcos said he would not meddle in the People’s Initiative signature probe and left validation to Comelec, which is evidence of procedural deference. | QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.6
- [PBBM stands by suspension of 139 NFA officials](/https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-stands-by-suspension-of-139-nfa-officials/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-03-06 | Claim: Marcos backed suspensions over anomalous rice sales and procedural irregularities, which cuts against shielding subordinates from scrutiny. | QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.7
- [Gov’t vows legal action vs deep-fake video creators, spreaders](/https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | Claim: The government treated the Marcos deepfake as an investigation/legal-action problem rather than a broad censorship sweep. | QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.7
- [Philippine News Agency: rice tariff review](/https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1227544) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-06-24 | Claim: NEDA said the rice tariff policy was under periodic review and could be tweaked if conditions changed, which is evidence of formal correction rather than hiding tradeoffs. | QIDs: 7B.8
- [PBBM signs laws on streamlining procurement, combatting online scams](/https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | Claim: Procurement reform and e-procurement were framed as reducing favoritism and graft, supporting a more rule-based public-finance posture. | QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.7

**Undercuts 7B.8**
- [Sona 2024 fact check](/https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964296/sona-2024-fact-check) | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | Claim: Marcos’s explanation that rice prices were mainly driven by external market forces was rated inaccurate; the fact-check says domestic policy also mattered, so the public framing was incomplete. | QIDs: 7B.8
- [$0.343/kilo rice still possible - Department of Agriculture, Philippines](/https://www.zawya.com/en/markets/commodities/0343-kilo-rice-still-possible-department-of-agriculture-philippines-vwstcm9g) | Reuters | 2024-07-24 | Claim: Reuters noted that P20 rice had been a campaign promise and that the administration was still trying to achieve it, showing the promise remained unmet midyear. | QIDs: 7B.8
- [No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it - PBBM](/https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-11-14 | Claim: Marcos refused independent ICC cooperation on the Duterte drug war unless Duterte consented, which is selective accountability rather than full openness. | QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.7, 7B.6
- [Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism](/https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | Claim: The country report says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted, and that the state flexed regulatory power over broadcasters, which weakens the case for transparent, good-faith governance. | QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.7, 7B.6
- [Philippines: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report](/https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House | 2024 | Claim: Freedom House says disinformation and vote buying distorted competition, campaign-finance rules were weak, and red-tagging persisted, all of which point to an environment where scrutiny is easier to evade. | QIDs: 7B.8, 7B.6, 7B.7

**Search gap**
- I did not find a strong 2024 primary source showing Marcos voluntarily opened SALNs, donor ledgers, or internal tradeoff memos to broad independent scrutiny.
- The best negative evidence is indirect: selective refusal of ICC cooperation, misleading public framing on rice, and a persistently manipulative media environment rather than a documented single cover-up event.
